newsitem.title: BELGIUM: RESEARCH ALERT - Salomon downgrades Solvay.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Salomon downgrades Solvay.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said in a research report it downgraded shares in Solvay to 'underperform' from 'hold' because of the deterioration in the Belgian chemicals and drugs company's peroxide and plastics outlook.
Predicting selling prices would slip with petrochemical feedstock prices in the second half of 1997, Salomon noted in the report that Solvay had a major exposure to this industry.
"We predict no earnings growth for the next few years as declining plastics margins offset rapid gains from pharma," the report dated June 16 said.

Salomon did not expect margin pressure in hydrogen peroxyde, caustic soda and soda ash to ease off soon. As a non-integrated plastics producer Solvay had suffered from higher ethylene and propylene prices, it noted.

Plastics were expected to turn down in 1998 and 1999. "A loss in this division is not out of the question," it said. But the plastics processing division would benefit from lower plastic raw material prices over the next few years.
